source.title: The Quantization Benefits of Residual-Free Transformers
source.authors: Yi-Ping Ji; Mahalakshmi Sabanayagam; Peyman Moghadam; Hemanth Saratchandran; Simon Lucey

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary sections, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests initialization and optimizer effects on residual-free transformer trainability, extending those questions to language transformers; it does not test CIFAR classification error or a depth sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss outcomes relevant to V4. Activation kurtosis, quantization accuracy, and cited prior-work results are not rows because they do not measure the training behavior named in the versions.
record.test_reason: The initialization ablations report training-loss outcomes in plain, residual-free language transformers, extending V4's signal-propagation and trainability question to a new architecture and task. They do not test the specific tanh or convolutional comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's optimization paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that orthogonal initialization and spectral or second-order optimization make moderately deep residual-free transformers trainable, with depth-aware temperature scaling improving convergence. Their central conclusion concerns near-Gaussian activations and improved quantization robustness, accompanied by a modest full-precision performance gap and unresolved scaling limits.
record.recipe_differences: Language-model pretraining on FineWeb-Edu with residual-free transformers and KL Shampoo/orthogonal initialization; not the image-classification initialization comparisons described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization, optimizer, attention normalization or temperature schedule, and learning rate affect reported training loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual-free transformers preserve near-Gaussian activations and withstand low-bit quantization better under the evaluated protocol.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual connectivity and the training recipe affect activation fourth moments and quantization robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: With orthogonal initialization fixed, KL Shampoo achieves lower training loss than SOAP and Muon, while Muon has higher throughput.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice changes convergence and computational throughput in residual-free transformers.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 is stated in the paper; supplied venue metadata is arXiv.org.
record.problems: Training results are single runs without training-seed error bars. The study evaluates one primary model size and depth for these ablations and does not report a depth sweep. The QK-normalization comparison is reported in text, while the temperature-scaling training-loss comparison is also shown in a figure.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on V4 were left out. Quantization, activation-statistic, and downstream-accuracy results do not measure V4's training-speed or trainable-depth claim.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/100 training classification error, random labels, and the effects of model size, regularization, or training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher–student optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent degradation in plain versus residual convolutional networks, longer-training controls, deep tanh networks, and Fixup.

Activation-matched initialization comparisons in the original network families; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights at matched variance; a trainable-depth sweep; very deep tanh networks; and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Initial linearized stability limits, above-threshold recovery, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, higher learning-rate tolerance attributable to batch normalization, and Fixup comparisons. RMSNorm and QK normalization do not test this version.

missing.what: The 730M-parameter residual-free model also trains stably with the proposed recipe at 24 layers. Record this qualitative trainability result separately from downstream and quantization accuracy; it extends the tested width, not depth, and does not isolate initialization.
missing.locator: Section E.11, Scaling to Larger Models

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. Default-initialization failure is a control, not a challenge to V4. The results establish conditional trainability rather than an initialization-only causal effect or a maximum trainable depth. Training outcomes are single runs; calibration-seed uncertainty does not quantify training variability.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth-dependent training error in plain versus residual convolutional networks, and the cited special initialization and Fixup comparisons.
Plain feedforward and convolutional networks; matched Gaussian versus orthogonal initialization at the same variance; trainable depth, including 10,000-layer networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization versus no normalization on the listed image benchmarks, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: Residual-Free transformer with default initialization and KL Shampoo
rows.operation_detail: Trained with default initialization and KL Shampoo at the listed learning rates.
rows.value: all tested learning rates exhibit an early plateau near 7.38 within the first 1,000 training steps
rows.locator: Section E.10, Trainability of residual-free models
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the three listed learning rates.
rows.check: The reported plateau is correct. This is a failed-training control with default initialization, not evidence against appropriately matched initialization. The text does not fully specify whether its temperature schedule matches R3.

source_check.locator_found: Section E.10, Trainability of residual-free models, lines 4974–4977; Section D for model dimensions and data.

rows.subject: Residual-Free transformer with orthogonal initialization and AdamW
rows.operation_detail: Trained with orthogonal initialization and AdamW.
rows.locator: Section E.10, Trainability of residual-free models
rows.note: The text identifies this as the best stable run; the complete recipe reaches a lower loss.
rows.check: The value is correct, but it is the best stable selected run. Its comparison with R3 changes the optimizer and may change temperature scaling; it shows limited training with this initialization–optimizer combination rather than isolating initialization's effect.

rows.subject: Residual-Free transformer with the complete recipe
rows.operation_detail: Trained with orthogonal initialization, KL Shampoo, and depth-aware temperature scaling.
rows.locator: Section E.10, Trainability of residual-free models
rows.note: Reported as the complete residual-free recipe result; the text does not state the step for this value here.
rows.check: The value is correct. It demonstrates trainability with the complete recipe, not an initialization-only improvement. Section E.10 does not specify the step corresponding to 2.67.

source_check.locator_found: Section E.10, lines 4978–4983; Sections 4 and D specify the complete recipe.

rows.subject: Residual-Free transformer with QK normalization
rows.operation_detail: Trained with QK normalization, orthogonal initialization, and KL Shampoo.
rows.value: plateaus near 7.4 within the first few hundred steps, with no subsequent improvement during the observed run
rows.locator: Section E.9, QK Normalization as an Alternative to Temperature Scaling
rows.note: The paper says QK normalization alone does not impose the depth schedule.
rows.check: Change partial to absent: the authors explicitly report an early plateau near 7.4 with no subsequent improvement. This is a condition where orthogonal initialization plus KL Shampoo fails with QK normalization; the matched comparison changes attention scaling, not initialization.

relationships.condition: 194M-parameter, 24-layer residual-free transformers trained with the complete initialization, optimizer, and temperature recipe
relationships.reason: R1 plateaus near NLL 7.38 with default initialization, whereas R3 reaches 2.67 with the complete recipe; this supports initialization-sensitive trainability, although the comparison does not isolate initialization.
relationships.display_finding: Default initialization plateaued near NLL 7.38, whereas the complete recipe reached 2.67, with initialization, optimizer and temperature changes combined.
